rosary as october, the month of the holy rosary, draws to a close, we turn towards november, a month dedicated to remembering & praying for our faithful departed loved ones. the rosary can be a prayer of love & remembrance. for many of our loved ones, the rosary beads may have rested in their hands in their final hours, as family members gathered around them, praying the familiar decades. those familiar prayers offered comfort, reminding them that they were not alone, but surrounded by love & held in faith. annual novena for the deceased at masses from sunday 1st — monday 9th november the annual novena for the deceased here in our parish runs from: sunday 1st to monday 9th november . altar lists of the deceased are available at the back of each church. these can be returned to either church before or during the novena. during mass times there will be a box located in front of the altar. otherwise leave them in the silver box at the altar. ——————————— - while the church puts great emphasis on remembering our loved ones throughout the year, special emphasis is placed on them during the month of november, which begins with the great solemnity of all saints / all hallows november 1st the commemoration of all the faithful departed or all souls on november 2nd. norms for indulgences at the commemoration of all souls 1. from twelve o’clock noon on 1st november until midnight on 2nd november, all who have confessed, received holy communion & prayed for the pope’s intentions (one our father & hail mary, or any other prayer of one’s choice) can gain one plenary indulgence by visiting a church or oratory, & there reciting one our father & the apostle’s creed. this indulgence is applicable only to the souls of the departed. confession may be made at any time within the week preceding or the week following the 1st of november. holy communion may be received on any day from 1st to 8th november. 2. the faithful who visit a cemetery & pray for the dead may gain a plenary indulgence applicable only to the holy souls on the usual conditions once per day from 1st to 8th november. the conditions mentioned above also apply for this. mass for the bereaved friday 13th november 7:30pm november is the month of remembering our deceased loved ones, but it is also an important time to reach out to those who grieve their loss. recent grief can be very hard to navigate, but many also carry a silent grief from years past. mass for people in the parish who have been bereaved & for all those who feel the pain of loss, heavy within them, will take place in athenry church friday 13th november at 7:30pm. this is a mass for both athenry & newcastle church areas. please inform anyone that may like to attend. “cuppa” after mass in pastoral centre diocesan funeral ministry the funeral ministry training programme will take place in 2027. if anyone else is interested in funeral ministry but hasn’t yet registered, you are still very welcome to join. it’s not too late! appreciated. louisburgh church restoration and repair works since 2015 the south wall of the church and the bel l tower have suffered from significant water penetration (a problem first noted in the 1950s). internal render is breaking down, and paintwork is peeling off the walls. humidity levels in the building are high and water saturation of walls is reducing thermal performance making the building difficult to heat and maintain. investigative repo rts were carried out to identify and remedy the sources of moisture penetration. these included a measurement survey and structural , stained glass, services, asbestos, and building condition reports. temporary screens were erected to test the performance of the wall structure. a specialist conservation contractor carried out drill testing o f the walls which confirmed significant water-logging of wall cores. a conservation management plan was commissioned to guide the remedial works and to aid in making applications for grant funding. in february 2026 an application was made to mayo county council for permission to carry out repair works to remedy wall damp initially on 2 bays of the west wall, replace the bell tower roof and resurface the gravel path connecting the two entrances. in november 2026 an application will be made to mayo county council for grant funding to carry out these works under the historic structures fund and it is intended to begin restoration works in 2027. the first irish national synodal assembly took place in gormanston, co. meath, on october 17th. over 300 lay people, priests, religious and thirtieth sunday in ordinary time to love the lord with all our heart – is this even possible? a common assumption is that love must just come, that it grows organically, and that it cannot be forced . that’s infatuation, not true love . any kind of love – for a parent, spouse, child, or friend – will reach a point during which it is no longer easy. for love to be true, it must be a free choice and commitment. ‘all your heart, soul, and mind’ sounds rather extreme, even rather dangerous. the world says that loving anyone totally is a risky proposition – what if the one we love rejects us or lets us down, leaving us with nothing? and the world is even more terrified to love god totally, who cannot even be seen. this makes sense; after all, to love totally is to trust that we will find fulfilment precisely by not looking for it ourselves, but by looking to fulfil someone else. that old, al most clichéd phrase, ‘love grows when it is given away ,’ is actually spot-on in this regard. true love takes a leap of faith, which is what frightens nonbelievers . many people are okay with going to church every now and then or volunteering for a charity from time to t ime(and posting it on instagram, of course). loving like that does not require us to make an y kind of leap, any kind of definitive change, any commitment. but loving god with everything means that all do is for love of him. we trust that he will take care of us. that is heroic; that is what it means to bea saint. intercom: epriest.com parish church guided holy hour : sunday from 7pm to 8pm. holy face devotion: tuesday at 3.30pm. adoration: monday 11am-12noon, tuesday 7pm-8pm, thursday, friday 11am-8pm. rosary, divine mercy chaplet: daily at 3pm. confessions: saturday 12pm – 1pm. the family centre, castlebar ecumenical service for those bereaved by suicide friday 6th november at 8pm, in the church of the holy rosary. all are welcome. adoration in the church of the holy rosary have you an hour to spend with jesus in the blessed sacrament?
